summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — TRV +9%, STX +6%, CNC +4%, CASY +4%, LITE +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (ISRG -14%, CDNS -9%, SNPS -8%, NFLX -7%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: ISRG (-14.14%) — Post-earnings selloff: Q2 beat (rev $2.89B vs est, EPS $2.80 vs $2.55) but soft US da Vinci system growth, a da Vinci component recall, and ACA-exchange coverage fears drove analyst price-target cuts and a multi-day slide. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — ISRG is a large-cap medtech/healthcare name, a sector likely excluded from the bot's tradable list; the move was also earnings-adjacent (reported 7/16), a window many bots blackout to avoid gap/IV risk.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 EPS of $10.26 core vs ~$5.34 est., combined ratio improved to 83.6% on sharply lower catastrophe losses, prompting a wave of price-target hikes (Raymond James to $400, Truist $395).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — TRV is a mega-cap P&C insurer/Dow component, a sector the bot's momentum/tech-leaning universe likely excludes entirely, so no filter ever got a chance to evaluate the post-earnings gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a financials/insurance sleeve (or a market-cap-based catch-all) to the universe with an earnings-gate rule that releases names showing post-results gap ≥5% and combined-ratio/EPS beat within the first session.

top_movers.catalyst: No earnings yet (due 7/28) — surge driven by a wave of bullish analyst price-target hikes (Wells Fargo, Citi, JPMorgan, Goldman, BNP Paribas) on AI-datacenter HDD demand optimism.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — likely excluded as a large-cap hardware/storage name not on the bot's tracked ticker list, so no filter ever got a chance to evaluate the move.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-agnostic watchlist trigger that flags names with ≥3 analyst price-target upgrades in 48h for universe inclusion, independent of the static ticker list.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide managed-care rally after a peer insurer beat and raised FY guidance, plus CNC's own Illinois Medicaid contract win and price-target hikes ahead of July 28 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CNC is a large-cap defensive managed-care/health insurer, a sector the bot's momentum/growth-tilted universe construction likely excludes entirely.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a healthcare-payer sector bucket (large-cap defensives) to the universe screen, or add a peer-earnings-reaction scanner that flags same-sector names moving in sympathy with a reporting peer.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued sell-side re-rating: KeyBanc, Deutsche Bank, BofA, Stephens all hiked targets (to $970-$1,000) after Q4/FY26 earnings beat and a new 400-store, 3-year expansion plan.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CASY is a ~$850/share, large-cap consumer-staples/convenience-retail name with historically low beta/ATR%, a profile that doesn't clear momentum or gap-based universe screens built around cheaper, higher-volatility tickers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a low-beta 'steady compounder' sleeve with a high per-share price cap (>$500) and long-lookback breakout trigger, so slow multi-week analyst-upgrade grinds like this qualify instead of being filtered out by price/volatility caps.

top_movers.catalyst: Q1 EPS $2.37 beat $2.27 est, revenue +90% YoY to $808M, strong Q4 guidance ($2.85-$3.05 EPS); multiple analysts (Rosenblatt, Stifel, Morgan Stanley) hiked price targets to $900-$1,300.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — LITE is a mid-cap optical/photonics component name (AI datacenter transceivers), a niche industrial/tech-component category likely not covered by the bot's large-cap or sector universes.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a mid-cap AI-infrastructure/optical-components bucket (e.g. names tied to 800G/1.6T transceiver supply chains) to the universe scanner so post-earnings gappers like LITE are screenable, gated by an earnings-beat + guidance-raise filter.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide managed-care rally—read-through from UnitedHealth's Q2 guidance hike (7/16) plus fresh analyst upgrades (Truist PT to $415, Zacks Strong Buy)—running ahead of HUM's own 7/29 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HUM is a large-cap, low-beta managed-care/health insurer, and momentum/news-reactive bots likely scope to higher-beta tech/consumer names rather than slow-moving, regulation-driven healthcare payors.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap managed-care payors (HUM, UNH, CVS, ELV, CNC, MOH) to the universe with a peer-correlation trigger that watchlists them after a sector bellwether's earnings-guidance surprise.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-earnings selloff: Q2 beat (rev $2.89B vs est, EPS $2.80 vs $2.55) but soft US da Vinci system growth, a da Vinci component recall, and ACA-exchange coverage fears drove analyst price-target cuts and a multi-day slide.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ISRG is a large-cap medtech/healthcare name, a sector likely excluded from the bot's tradable list; the move was also earnings-adjacent (reported 7/16), a window many bots blackout to avoid gap/IV risk.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-drift scanner that re-admits names 2-4 sessions after an earnings gap if the move persists ≥2 days in one direction, and review whether healthcare/medtech large-caps should be added to the universe given ISRG's liquidity.

top_movers.catalyst: No earnings surprise (Q2 report due 7/27) — stock fell on sector-wide AI-capex-sustainability fears days after Cadence's own AuraStack AI launch, as investors trimmed richly-valued AI/EDA names (~42x forward earnings).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CDNS is a large-cap EDA/design-software name, a sector the bot's tradable universe doesn't currently cover, so no filter ever saw the move to act on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EDA/semiconductor-design-software (CDNS, SNPS, ANSS) to a large-cap sector-momentum or valuation-derating universe so multi-day AI-capex-fear selloffs in this cohort become screenable, not just chip/hardware names.

top_movers.catalyst: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 autonomous chip-design demo spooked investors about AI disrupting Synopsys' EDA moat, capping a 5-day ~$12B/13.7% slide.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SNPS is large-cap EDA/semiconductor-design software, a sector not covered by current tech/semis screens; also a multi-day thematic grind rather than a single-day gap a news-reactive bot would key off.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EDA/chip-design software names (SNPS, CDNS) to the semis-adjacent universe and add a thematic-risk tag for 'AI disintermediation' headlines to flag multi-day moat-erosion selloffs, not just single-day gaps.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued post-earnings slide: Q2 beat but weak Q3 guidance + cut transparency (dropping quarterly engagement reports) triggered multi-day analyst price-target cuts (TD Cowen, BofA, Rosenblatt) after the 7/16 report.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — NFLX is a large-cap media/streaming name likely excluded by an earnings-blackout or elevated-realized-volatility screen post-gap, not a technical filter miss within an included universe.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-drift override: allow names with a ≥5% earnings-day gap plus follow-on analyst price-target cuts within 3 trading days to re-enter the eligible universe for a short-biased or fade-the-drift setup, bypassing the standard earnings-blackout exclusion.
